title: Outside the Fence
subtitle: The lambs know not the purpose of the fence.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Whuu ... phew ...
First, the child self, then the teenage self, and then the young adult self. Only in the Meditator's Realm can one face so many past selves ...
... and defeat them one after another.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: The 20-year-old me was fierce.
Kaalaa Baunaa rubs her bruised cheeks.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: *hiss* That pain feels real.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: You came here sooner than I expected, Kaalaa Baunaa.
The wind feels like tingling knives on the rooftop. A familiar, if not too familiar, figure once again emerges in front of her.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: I knew you would come.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Kumar.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Finally. See you again.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: I miss you dearly, too, my child. I hope you've been doing well while I was away.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Hope you're happy with the surroundings I set. I always find it enjoyable here—a place full of memories and perfect for small talks.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: I'd rather you suffered, Miss.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Ah, someone is having a worse attitude these days.
Kaalaa Baunaa looks around to observe the surroundings.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: There's no need to look around, kid. I already had a few years of experience in the field before you started your research. And one of the most basic skills one has to master in the Meditator's Realm is to cover up the traces of reality.
The sky is dark, like the surface of dusted glassware.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Even so, you didn't even think about creating a starry sky for yourself here.
Kumar is silent for a moment and then shakes her head.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Hmm. That would be unnecessary. You can see it any time outside this Realm if you like.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Why did you "invite" me here?

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: I know you've put in a lot of efforts. I understand the difficulty within and sympathize with you, Kaalaa Baunaa. I always do, just like what I did with my younger brother. By the way, that letter has been delivered to him safely, I assume?

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: You're smart enough not to bring the Vishnu statue with you. Did somebody kindly remind you not to do that?

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Never mind. That's not helpful.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: I don't understand. Why involve him?
Behind Kumar, an old finderscope is aiming at the sky.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Emm, maybe I was being vindictive out of "hatred," like you said.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: After all, they precluded me from doing anything even before I gave it a try. Although my misfortune was not my brother's doing, there's no one else left in the family to take my anger.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: So ask me now. Ask me anything you wish to know. I can tell you everything. What you're curious about, what you're confused about, anything you can't work out in your little brain. I can explain it all.
She smiles warmly, but her words are as cold as usual.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Hasn't the idea that I might locate you bothered you for even a second?
Kaalaa Baunaa takes a tentative step forward.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Locate me? Hahaha. You are still as naive as a child, my Kaalaa Baunaa. You little dummy owl. That is simply impossible.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: This is the first time you doubt my capability.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: No, why would I do that? Of all the students, you are the only child who is smart enough to follow my steps this far.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: You just don't have time on your side and need a better mindset in dealing with the unexpected.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: I've tried to teach it to you. Remember those impromptu speeches I asked you to give? Those were good practice.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: "Don't have ..." What do you mean?

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Perhaps you have put too much stock in the idea that I will rely on Manus Vindictae in this. Instead, I trust myself more than them. And, of course, I also trust you.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: What's more, they were never good enough for me. But luckily, I have never been a real arcanist or a real human, only pretending to be either of them when necessary. I can easily act like an arcanist to gain their trust, just like I could act like a human when I was teaching at Banner.
Kumar notices that Kaalaa Baunaa has been staring at the old finderscope.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: What are you staring at? Take it if you're interested.
Kumar takes off the finderscope and throws it lightly to Kaalaa Baunaa. It lands precisely on her palm.
The surroundings remain the same. Kaalaa Baunaa can't find any loopholes at all.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: What? You thought it is the key to cracking the Meditator's Realm, like those stone statues earlier?

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Though it is too late for hints, there is one thing I have to remind you of.
She is indeed as thoughtful as she claims to be.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: You didn't catch up to "the real me," nor did you improve the situation by entering the Realm. You chased me all the way here, chased the hope of "winning" against me, but you only helped me complete my plan.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: The moment you entered the Realm, the last step of my plan was done.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: I completed what?

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: As you know, exerting influence on reality through the Meditator's Realm is challenging. After all, this Realm is like the shadow of its real counterpart, a reflection of reality.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: I went to a lot of trouble, even wasted a statue, to finally stick out a corner of the shadow over the boundary of the two worlds.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: You mean the statue in the cave ...

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: What I needed was an outside-in force to break the Realm, which is almost unbreakable from the inside.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: A mirror can reflect objects, but there's nothing it can do to itself. It can only be shattered into pieces by people not from the reflection, but reality.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Whenever there is a shooting star streaking across the sky of this Realm,

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: an equally beautiful star will fall on the real earth!

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: And guess what? YOU are the force I'm looking for.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: No. How?

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: So the fluctuation I detected, the energy of the celestial body felt by the Foundation girl ... are just false alert?

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Oh, no, I have to admit, that young girl was not part of my plan. But, at least, you are on the right track about what happened!

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: If anything is to blame, it's your ego. You were trying to win, but not by saving people. The idea of proving yourself to me outweighed their lives.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: You must be wondering, "How could she lay such a trap with her insignificant arcane power"?

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: "She can barely lift a lump of clay. She must have had the Manus Vindictae on her side to help!"

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: All that being said, you don't have to feel yourself to be a lesser version of me. You're still my best student, my best colleague, and my strongest rival—well, with some room to improve.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Even this time, you didn't lose the game for lack of wits, but for the fact that I know you a bit better than you know me,

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: and I simply have more experience hunting a prey.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: You and the Manus ... I've never, never thought that.
Kaalaa Baunaa feels her explanation is meaningless and stuck in her throat. She's almost choking for breath in the gentle breeze.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: That means if I didn't enter the Realm to see you ...

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Then things are going to be tricky for me. You would be enjoying a happy Dīpa Festival, while I would be crying in a dark corner nobody knows of.

items.speaker: Kaalaa Baunaa
items.text: Why? Why would you ...?

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Well, time's up. Remember to ask the most important question first next time, child.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Don't thank me for that suggestion, and don't think too much of my kindness. I didn't explain all these things for your sake. I told you everything, because only by doing so can I enjoy the victory to its fullest. Your desperation is a good prize for me.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: You know I have a bad taste for entertainment.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Go back to the Dīpa Festival. At least there's one good thing left for you—you will get to see that beautiful shooting star with your own eyes, just like I will.

items.speaker: Kumar
items.text: Goodbye.
